Hi Alice — thanks for the note. Short answer up front: by default, Redwood does NOT train our public models on customer inference traffic. Below I summarize the standard position and the common exceptions so you can include the language in your compliance materials.

Summary (one-line): Redwood does not use customer inference traffic to train or improve our hosted models unless a customer explicitly opts into a separate model-training/finetuning program or submits data for a managed tuning engagement.

Details and nuances:
- Hosted API (default): inference requests and embeddings are isolated; we do not add customer inputs to our general training corpus. We retain request metadata and transient logs for operational reasons (see retention below) but those are not used for model training.
- Dedicated capacity: customer workloads run on reserved capacity and are treated as data-isolated; no training on that traffic.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customers manage their data and models; Redwood does not access or train on that data unless explicitly contracted.
- Opt-in programs: we offer paid tuning and dataset ingestion programs where customers explicitly consent and contract for model training or supervised fine-tuning; these are always documented, access-controlled, and billable.

Retention and deletion highlights (typical defaults):
- Short-term request logs and telemetry: retained 30 days by default; used for debugging, rate-limiting, and cost telemetry.
- Audit logs (security/change logs): retained 90 days by default, configurable for enterprise customers via Dedicated/Private options.
- KV caches/prefix caches: ephemeral (kept in-memory or on accelerated ephemeral storage) and purged per deployment restart; not persisted in long-term backups in standard hosted plans.
- Backups/snapshots: backups are encrypted and rotated; deleted records are removed from live stores immediately and from backups as part of the next backup rotation window (varies by disk snapshot cadence, typically 7–14 days).
- Deletion requests: we process customer deletion requests within 72 hours for live data; complete removal from all backup rotations is dependent on snapshot cadence but we provide an ERASED confirmation when the data is removed from long-term backups.

I'll loop in our privacy/legal folks for the final standardized wording you can include in contracts and the vendor assessment. Attaching a short security overview and SOC2 pointer now.

Best,

Thanks — quick legal-approved language below. I've kept it clear and narrow to avoid overpromising. Vivek, flag if infra needs tighter bounds on "backup rotation" wording.

Legal-approved single-line guarantee (safe-for-contract text):
"Redwood does not use customer inference traffic (API requests, file uploads, or embeddings) to train or improve our public models unless the customer explicitly opts into a paid training or fine-tuning engagement."

Supplemental bullets (can be used in security questionnaires):
- Retention: live request logs are retained 30 days by default; audit logs retained 90 days. Customers on Dedicated or Private plans may request extended retention settings via contract.
- Caches: prefix/KV caches are ephemeral and not persisted to our long-term model-training stores.
- Deletion: upon an authenticated deletion request we remove the data from live systems within 72 hours; removal from on-disk backups occurs according to snapshot rotation (typical window 7–14 days).
- Exceptions: any model training using customer data requires explicit, documented customer consent and a signed statement of work; access is limited to a small number of authorized engineers and is billable.
